claims.text: Reducing PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticle size from approximately 6 nm to approximately 2 nm increases the fraction of undercoordinated surface atoms.
The increased fraction of undercoordinated atoms modifies the adsorption energies of ethanol and its reaction intermediates.
Reducing PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticle size from approximately 6 nm to approximately 2 nm enhances ethanol-oxidation activity.
Reducing PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticle size from approximately 6 nm to approximately 2 nm alters ethanol-oxidation product selectivity.
The baseline material is a polyol-synthesized, approximately 6 nm PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalyst.
Adjusting synthesis temperature and surfactant concentration can produce PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts with mean diameters of approximately 2, 4, and 6 nm.
Changing nanoparticle size changes surface curvature.
Greater surface curvature increases the proportion of undercoordinated sites.
In situ XPS and IR spectroscopy can confirm changes in undercoordinated active-site density.
A higher density of low-coordination sites modifies the catalyst's electronic structure.
Adsorption of molecules and reaction intermediates on a catalyst surface affects catalytic activity.
The size-induced adsorption changes cause shifts between partial and complete ethanol oxidation.
Approximately 2 nm particles will yield a higher prevalence of partial-oxidation products than approximately 6 nm particles.
Approximately 4 nm particles will exhibit activity and selectivity intermediate between those of approximately 2 nm and approximately 6 nm particles.
The proposed size mechanism applies over a particle-size range of approximately 2–6 nm in acidic electrolyte at 25–80 degrees Celsius when composition is held constant.
Alloy compositional heterogeneity may overlap with or confound nanoparticle-size effects on activity and selectivity.
